messages.subject: Collexeme Analysis: Interpreting Delta p Scores
messages.subject_clean: Collexeme Analysis: Interpreting Delta p Scores
messages.body_plain:
Hello and Happy Holidays!

I'm working on a collexeme analysis of abstract noun use and the immediate lexicogrammatical patterns in which the nouns occur with NS and ELL groups. I wanted to be sure I correctly understand the results with Coll.analysis 3.5.

After I process a table and read results in a .doc file, the Delta p scores are confusing (delta.p.constr.to.word). I think the reason is that the explanation preceding the results is worded this way:

"delta.p.constr.to.word: delta p: how much does the word/construction help guess the word?
delta.p.constr.to.word: delta p: how much does the construction help guess the word/construction?"

Is this instead supposed to read the following way:

"delta.p.constr.to.word: delta p: how much does the construction help guess the word?
delta.p.word to constr.: delta p: how much does the word help guess the construction?"

I've been interpreting the delta p score as a one-directional attraction score, assuming that, as with the FYE attraction score, significance  of p<.001 is reached with a score of 3 or greater. Is that an accurate interpretation?

I thank you for your time!

Brian

messages.body_plain:
> I've been interpreting the delta p score as a one-directional attraction score, assuming that, as with the FYE attraction score, significance  of p<.001 is reached with a score of 3 or greater. Is that an accurate interpretation?

Sorry--I meant to say that I've been interpreting delta p as something like a percentage. So a word-to-pattern score of .9 (90%) would indicate that the word is highly predictive of the pattern.

messages.subject_clean: [CorpLing with R] Re: Collexeme Analysis: Interpreting Delta p Scores
messages.body_plain:
The explanation may not be phrased in the best way but I think in the
new coll.analysis script - the one that avoids the Inf issue for
superhigh attractions - it's probably better. Using the collexeme
analysis example from website (http://tinyurl.com/collostructions>)
(ditransitives in ICE-GB):

give.in.ditrans <- matrix(c(461,699,574,136930), ncol=2,
                          dimnames=list(CX=c("ditrans","other"),
VERB=c("give","other")))
delta.p(give.in.ditrans) # function on my system
# $Overview
# [1] "If +outcome and +cue is in the top left cell, then ..."
#
# $`Delta P for the cue in the columns and the outcome in the rows`
# [1] 0.3932394
#
# $`Delta P for the cue in the rows and the outcome in the columns`
# [1] 0.4403318

# The coll.analysis output has this heading now:
# delta.p.word.cues.constr: delta p: how much does the word cue the
construction?
# delta.p.constr.cues.word: delta p: how much does the construction
help cue the word?
# and
# - the column "delta.p.word.cues.constr" is p(ditrans|give) - p
(ditrans|other v), i.e.
give.in.ditrans[1,1] / colSums(give.in.ditrans)[1] - # 0.3974138
give.in.ditrans[2,1] / colSums(give.in.ditrans)[2]   # 0.005083488
# 0.3923303

# - the column "delta.p.constr.cues.word" is p(give|ditrans) - p
(give|other cx), i.e.
give.in.ditrans[1,1] / rowSums(give.in.ditrans)[1] - # 0.4454106
give.in.ditrans[2,1] / rowSums(give.in.ditrans)[2]   # 0.005078871
# 0.4403318

HTH,
STG
--
Stefan Th. Gries
----------------------------------
Univ. of California, Santa Barbara
http://tinyurl.com/stgries
----------------------------------
